svg.title: APEX 26.1 and SQLcl 26.1 project upgrade flow — version 5
svg.desc: A detailed flowchart showing preparation, baseline creation, production drift handling, APEXlang validation, clean deployment, regression testing, concurrent feature incorporation, production-first cutover, merge, and cleanup.
svg.text: A production-safe path from the current project line to a tested, deployable 26.1 baseline

g.text: Workflow-defining constraint: APEX applications move forward only
Current-line applications can move into the 26.1 clone.
Applications exported from 26.1 cannot move back.

svg.text: Keep the current DEV / TEST / PROD line available on APEX 24.2 and SQLcl 25.4.

text.tspan: Clone PROD when possible, or assemble
matching metadata plus production APEX apps.
or clean it reliably between deployments.
Make that folder select SQLcl 26.1 while
the current project continues on SQLcl 25.4.

svg.text: Regenerate source, reconcile production drift, compile APEXlang, stage, and prove a clean installation.

g.text: Full database export — exclude APEX apps
Delete generated database source → run project export
Database objects / PL/SQL only — not APEXlang
Article 06 · full export if synonyms are involved
Use the custom alias / APEX export workaround
SQLcl 26.1 project export corrupts binary application files
Fix on the current APEX line
The affected 26.1 page may not open in Builder
Validation passed → import is expected to succeed
Create and review the first 26.1 release
Replay the complete SQLcl Project history
Record baseline changesets without applying them
Test deeply while production development continues
Functional testing is project-defined; every production release must also be reconciled into the upgrade line.
Test behavior—not merely validation or rendering
Older Flow for APEX package failed;
Reset/deploy VM and repeat the test
MANDATORY WHEN A PRODUCTION FEATURE ARRIVES
APEX 24.2 / SQLcl 25.4 release becomes main history
2 · Deliver the same release to clone
Clone receives the exact PROD changeset identities
3 · Merge APEX apps in the clone
Working Copy preserves and reapplies 26.1 corrections
Restore release + changelog; export related objects
Verify the feature and every earlier 26.1 correction
Cut over in a tight, quiet maintenance window
Upgrade PROD first; use the clone as temporary DEV until DEV and TEST catch up.
Baseline and prior PROD releases are already recorded
Only until normal DEV/TEST are upgraded
Conflict rule: preserve the upgrade branch’s reconciled 26.1 state—not a positional “ours/theirs” label.
If main contains an unincorporated business change, stop and run the feature-incorporation loop before completing the merge.
The resettable VM may remain as reusable deployment-test infrastructure.
